english: Do you live near the river? I live here with my wife, and I have three sons. What do they do? The older ones row the boat; the young one guards our cattle. Guest, do you have sons? english: Why did you throw your knife into the current? I gave it to the god of the waters. Tomorrow we cross the boundary: may the god guard us. Does he want copper? He wants the best things. Then I will give him my spear. Do not give the spear: beyond the boundary there are enemies. Then I will sing him a song. The god will hear it.

english: Girl, give me water; I am thirsty. Drink from the stream: it is full. It is not sweet; give me your cup. Why are you here, stranger? I sell salt in the villages. Then drink, and be well. What is your name, girl? Ask my father! He sits at the fire.

english: Mistress, do you not fear the river? It is deep and swift. I was born beside it; my mother taught me to cross the water. Do you have children? I have two daughters; they are swifter than the boys. Where is your husband? He went downstream in a boat; he will trade hides by the sea.

english: Grandfather, sing me a hymn for the river. The river flows from the spring to the sea. It feeds the fish, and it holds up the boats. At night it does not sleep. Is it not tired? It is not tired: it is immortal. Sing it again, grandfather! I will sing it, and you will sleep.

english: Woman, the river has grown great: it rained for three days. Where are your cattle? We drove them away from the water. The water is coming to our houses. Help me: carry the children out! I will carry them. Where shall we take them? To the great oak: the water has not reached it. May the gods guard the children!

english: Grandmother, tell me a story about the otter. An otter lived in the stream. She ate the men's fish, and they grew angry. They set a net in the water; the otter tore it with her teeth and fled. Did they catch her? They did not catch her. She still swims in our stream. Tomorrow I will look for her. Look for her, and do not throw stones at her!

english: When will you come back from the trade? I will come back when the new moon grows bright. What are you carrying downstream? Grain and honey. With them I will buy gold. The river is swift below the village: guard yourself! I know it; last year I crossed it twice. Bring me gold from the trade! I will bring you gold, my dear.

english: Mistress, I have come from a far land by water. Dear guest, be well! Where is your boat? I bound it at the oak with a rope. Sit at the fire; my daughter will bring you mead. May the gods give you good things. Tell me: what have you seen on the river? I have seen many boats; men carry hides down to the sea.

english: Old man, did you catch many fish today? I caught few fish: my net broke. How did it break? A great sheatfish pulled it into the deep water, and then it fled. I will weave you a new net. You are a good young man! Weave it this evening, and early in the morning we two will go to the river.

english: Sister, teach me, and I will swim in the river. Are you not afraid of the water? I am not afraid. Then come into the water with me. Stretch out your hands and move your feet. english: Man, where is my son? Your son fell into the water. Is he alive? He is alive. I saw him in the current and pulled him out. Where is he now? He sits by my fire, and my wife warms him. You are dear to me; may the gods give you good things! Do not weep, woman. Come and see your son.

english: Woman, what did you do today? At dawn I went to the river with my sister. We two drew the nets and caught many fish. Then we dried them in the sun. What did you do, guest? I walked by the stream and saw a beaver. The beaver builds his house in the water. He is a wise beast. He is wiser than my husband!

english: You pulled me out of the water. Who are you? I dwell beyond the river. Your villagers are our enemies. Today I am not your enemy. I saw a man in the current, and I pulled him up. What shall I give you? Give me nothing. Do not forget me. I will not forget you. My brothers will not fight against you.

english: My oxen fear the river; they do not step into it. Lead a cow first; the oxen will follow her. I have no cow here. Take my cow; she knows the ford. What do you want for her? Drive her back at dawn, and give me a pot of grain. I will do so at dawn. May you be fortunate!

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Grandmother, it is freezing; I will go across over the ice. Do not cross! The ice is thin. Yesterday my brother crossed it and did not go under. Yesterday it was cold; today the sun is warm. Then how shall I reach my sheep? Go down to the bridge, and walk on the thick ice. You are wise, grandmother. I am old; the old know the ice.

english: Neighbour, why is your net at my stakes? The gods gave the river to all men. My father set these stakes; they are the boundary. In spring the current carried off your stakes. Then I will set new stakes. Set them, and I will throw my net beyond them. You are a bad neighbour! Come in the evening, and we two will drink mead.

english: Man, let me into your boat; I am a bold warrior. A bold one? Then swim! I do not swim: the water is cold. You do fear it! I fear nothing! I killed three wolves. Wolves do not live in the water. Give me copper. Do not rock it! Be silent, bold one: here the current is strong.

english: Father, why do we two go to the water at night? At night the fish come to the fire. Hold the fire over the water, and I will strike them with the spear. I see a fish! It is big. Be silent, or it will flee. Did you strike it? I struck it. Your mother will cook it at dawn.

english: Sister, show me how you weave a net. Take this cord and bind it with the other one. I have bound it. Is it pretty? It is pretty. Now bind a hundred others. My hands will grow tired! If you do not weave, we will not eat fish. Then I will weave all day.
